newsitem.title: UK: RMC, Redland down on Germany worries.
newsitem.headline: RMC, Redland down on Germany worries.

text.p: Shares in RMC Group Plc and Redland Plc dropped on Thursday amid fresh worries about weakness of the German economy and the impact of a strong pound on their overseas earnings, traders and analysts said.
RMC was down 26p at 10.20-1/2 by 0930 GMT, after touching a four-month low of 10.18 stg and Redland was down 9-1/2p at 414 after setting a four-month low of 411p.
"We were quite a big seller of RMC earlier in the week and there still seems to be quite a bit of stock around," said one trader.
Said another: "There is an overhang of stock and the strength of sterling is very much a concern. And there is a reflex reaction in these two any time anyone says anything about Germany."

Earlier, German figures showed the jobless total topping the four million mark for the first time in October. The German labour office said the economy was not growing strongly enough to curb unemployment significantly through 1997.
Both RMC and Redland have significant activities in Germany.
"All we need now is a poor winter," said Robin Hardy, analyst at Panmure Gordon. "Then we could have some major reductions in forecasts and people are beginning to get concerned about that."
